identity.title: Interpretation of ALMA velocity map for the obscuring torus in NGC1068

paper_type_evidence.quote: In the framework of N-body simulations we consider a dynamical model of an obscuring torus which accounts for the gravitational interaction between the clouds moving in the field of the central mass.

question.value: Can an N-body dynamical model of a self-gravitating clumpy torus reproduce the ALMA velocity map of the NGC1068 torus and give the SMBH mass?

evidence.loc: abstract
evidence.quote: The self-gravity of the torus induces the velocity distribution of clouds with a global orbital motion which mimics the ALMA data for NGC1068.

evidence.loc: ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS
evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA$\sharp$2016.1.00052.S.

evidence.loc: Introduction
evidence.quote: The next cycle of the ALMA observation was made with better resolution, in the molecules HCN and HCO$^+$ (Imanishi et al. 2018)

what.value: ALMA mean velocity map of the NGC1068 torus (observed, compared to model)

evidence.loc: Dynamics of the clouds in the torus and interpretation of ALMA results
evidence.quote: The mean velocity distribution of the ALMA data (Fig.[3](#fig:vel_map); left) clearly shows the global rotation of the matter

what.value: Observed velocity 20 km/s at 3 pc, inclination 34 deg

method.value: Rotate torus by two Euler angles, 30x30 cells, mean velocity of first 10 clouds along line of sight per cell

evidence.loc: Dynamics of the clouds in the torus and interpretation of ALMA results
evidence.quote: Find the mean velocity of the clouds which are located in the cylinder along the line of sight with the cross-section corresponding to the cell but taking into account only the first 10 clouds

results_numeric.quantity: SMBH mass in NGC1068 from model

evidence.loc: Conclusions
evidence.quote: The SMBH mass in NGC1068 is about $5 \times 10^6 M_\odot$.

evidence.loc: Conclusions
evidence.quote: The best match of the model velocity map with the observed one occurs for an inclination of the torus of $35^\circ$ from edge-on position.

findings_qualitative.value: Self-gravity with eccentric orbits explains low ALMA velocities with a higher SMBH mass than Keplerian estimate

evidence.loc: Dynamics of the clouds in the torus and interpretation of ALMA results
evidence.quote: Such low velocity for more high value of the SMBH mass is related to the fact that clouds move in eccentric orbits due to self-gravity of the torus

claims.hypothesis: A self-gravitating clumpy torus model reproduces the ALMA velocity map of NGC1068
claims.experiment: N-body simulation projected into 30x30 velocity maps at various orientations
claims.result: Orientation about 35 deg from edge-on matches the observed map
claims.finding: Orientation effects and clumpy structure explain the map

evidence.loc: Conclusions
evidence.quote: The velocity distribution in the torus of NGC1068 obtained by ALMA can be explained by orientation effects and clumpy structure.

claims.hypothesis: The SMBH mass is reconciled between megamaser and ALMA estimates
claims.experiment: Compare model velocity at 3 pc with 20 km/s
claims.finding: Keplerian estimate of 9e5 Msun is too low

evidence.loc: Dynamics of the clouds in the torus and interpretation of ALMA results
evidence.quote: the observational low velocity of the clouds (20 km/s at the distance 3 pc) can be explained by the SMBH mass $5 \times 10^6 M_\odot$

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Keplerian disk interpretation gives SMBH mass inconsistent with megamaser value

evidence.loc: Introduction

evidence.loc: Introduction

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparison with the ALMA map is qualitative only
No uncertainty on mass or inclination
Only 8192 clouds, with mass scaling argued rather than tested
Degeneracy between orientation and M_BH not explored
